messages.subject: [Advised Action] Migrate to Swift Package Manager for continued access to Google Maps Platform iOS SDKs
messages.full_content:
Hello Google Maps Platform customer,

To streamline our development and release processes, and align with the  
evolving iOS ecosystem, we will be phasing out support for CocoaPods as an  
installation method for our Google Maps Platform iOS SDKs.

What you need to know

Key changes:

We will stop releasing new versions of the following Google Maps Platform  
iOS SDKs through CocoaPods:

    - Maps SDK for iOS[1]
    - Places SDK for iOS[2]
    - Navigation SDK for iOS[3]
    - Fleet Engine[4]

CocoaPods is in maintenance mode[5], and Swift Package Manager has become  
the preferred dependency manager for iOS development. Focusing on Swift  
Package Manager will allow us to dedicate more resources to improving the  
SDKs.

We will support releasing new Google Maps Platform iOS SDKs versions (for  
example: version 10.x.x) through CocoaPods until Q2 2026. Starting with  
version 11.0 of all Google Maps Platform iOS SDKs, new versions will not be  
released on CocoaPods.

Potential impact:

If you continue to use CocoaPods after Q2 2026, you will not be able to  
access the latest Google Maps Platform iOS SDKs versions, including new  
features, performance improvements, and critical bug fixes.

What you need to do

Advised actions:

We encourage all developers currently using CocoaPods for Google Maps  
Platform iOS SDKs to begin planning their migration to Swift Package  
Manager or manual installation to ensure continued access to the latest  
updates. Learn more about the Swift Package Manager installation  
instructions in the SDK documentation links above.

Impacted customers/accounts:

You are using the affected SDKs on the following projects, format  
project_id (project_number):

    - avid-truth-434123-e0 (167887354208)

You may or may not be using CocoaPods in applications linked to those  
projects - only applications using CocoaPods are affected.

We’re here to help

We understand these changes may take some planning. If you have any  
questions or require assistance, please feel free to contact our support  
team at Google Maps Platform Support[6].

Thanks for choosing Google Maps Platform.

—The Google Maps Platform Team

[1] https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/ios-sdk/config
[2] https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/ios-sdk/config
[3]  
https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/navigation/ios-sdk/xcode-setup
[4] https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/mobility/fleet-engine
[5] https://blog.cocoapods.org/CocoaPods-Support-Plans/
[6]  
https://developers.google.com/maps/support/?utm_source=em-anncmt&utm_medium=em

messages.subject: Important update: Introducing Credits as our new billing unit
messages.full_content:
( https://www.make.com/en?utm_campaign=credits-launch-1308&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customer.io )
Hey Rich,

 

We’re writing to let you know about an important billing update.

 

Starting August 27, 2025, operations will be replaced by credits as the new billing unit. Most actions will consume 1 credit per action, advanced features (especially AI) consume more, either with a fixed cost or based on usage, providing a pricing model that better reflects your specific usage.

Here's what you need to know

Automatic conversion: No action is required from you. On August 27, your existing operations balance will be automatically converted to credits at a 1:1 rate: 1 Operation = 1 Credit.

Plan and price: Your current plan and price stay exactly the same. Both manual and automatic purchases of extra credits will work the same way as before.

Credit consumption: Most actions will consume 1 credit per action, advanced features (especially AI) consume more, either with a fixed cost or based on usage.

While operations will no longer be a billing unit, they will still be visible within your scenario execution, now representing your data unit processed. 

 

For more information about this change and how credits work, please visit our help documentation ( https://help.make.com/credits?utm_campaign=credits-launch-1308&utm_medium=email&utm_source=customer.io ). If you have any questions, don't hesitate to reach

messages.subject: Meet Ask AI, the built-in teammate for your apps 💬
messages.full_content:
( https://studio.softr.io/dashboard )
Introducing Ask AI: the built-in teammate for your Softr apps

Hi Rich,

Ask AI is the built-in teammate that reads live data and answers your end users' questions—right inside your app.

✅ Get instant answers: Your users can ask questions like “What’s overdue?” or “How many items are left in stock?” and get answers instantly, based on your app’s real-time data.
✅ No setup needed: Just toggle it on. No need to connect APIs or manage complicated settings.
✅ Customize it: Add instructions, set the tone, and guide the kinds of questions users can ask.

✅ Secure by default: Ask AI respects your visibility and permission rules (only has access to the data that each user can see).

How do I set it up? 
Just head to any dynamic block, click Actions, and add Ask AI as a topbar button. You can pick an icon, write custom instructions, and tailor the experience to match your app and users.

Is it available on the free plan? 
Yes! For now, Ask AI is available with unlimited usage on all plans, including Free. Soon, each plan will include a set number of monthly AI credits, and Ask AI will count toward those.

Note: Ask AI works with Softr Databases, Google Sheets, Notion, monday.com, ClickUp, Coda and more. Airtable, HubSpot, and SQL support coming soon.

Explore Ask AI ( https://www.softr.io/ask-ai )Want to see Ask AI in action? Check out the launch video ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tcsnnZHBFV8 ). 

Thanks for building with us!

- Mariam, CEO, Softr

messages.subject: [Product Update] New security enhancement for your Google Cloud environment
messages.full_content:
Re-authentication will be required for sensitive actions starting July 2025.




MY CONSOLE




Hello Rich,

We're reaching out with an important update regarding enhancing the  
security of sensitive actions in your Google Cloud environment. This update  
strengthens protection against unauthorized access to your critical Google  
Cloud resources.

We have provided additional information below to guide you through this  
change.

What you need to know

Key changes

Starting in July 2025, to further protect your critical Google Cloud  
resources, you will need to re-enter your password or complete multi-factor  
authentication (MFA) for certain sensitive actions. These actions include  
billing assignment changes and IAM policy changes at the Organization,  
Folder, or Project level.

This additional authentication step ensures that only authorized users can  
make critical changes to billing and access control settings.

Re-authentication limitations

This re-authentication will initially apply to Google Cloud Console users  
with Google Cloud Identity. It will not apply to programmatic user account  
access or external identities federated through Workforce Identity pools  
and SSO.

Actions that require re-authentication

Specifically, you will be prompted to re-authenticate when performing the  
following actions (which correspond to these API calls):


resourcemanager.organizations.setIamPolicy
resourcemanager.folders.setIamPolicy
resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy
billing.accounts.setIamPolicy
billing.accounts.move
billing.accounts.removeFromOrganization
billing.resourceAssociations.create
billing.resourceAssociations.delete
resourcemanager.projects.deleteBillingAssignment
resourcemanager.projects.createBillingAssignment
resourcemanager.tagValueBindings.delete

Note: Service accounts are not affected by these new re-authentication  
requirements.

What you need to do

No action is required from you. This enhanced security will be  
automatically applied starting July 2025.

We're here to help

You can find more details about Reauthentication for Sensitive Actions in  
our User Guide. If you have any questions or require assistance, please  
contact reauth-for-sensitive-actions@google.com.

Thank you for your understanding and cooperation as we work to improve  
security in Google Cloud.

Thanks for choosing Google Cloud.





— The Google Cloud Team





DOCUMENTATION



SUPPORT

messages.subject: Update: Deprecating scores in Auto search
messages.full_content:
Hey there,

We’re rolling out a major improvement to Auto search in our API. The new architecture doesn’t create meaningful relevance scores for results. As a result, we’re deprecating scores in Auto search on June 18th.

If your app uses Auto search scores, we recommend migrating as soon as possible. You can read more about search types in our docs here ( https://docs.exa.ai/reference/exas-capabilities-explained#search-types ).
Note: Scores in Neural search results will remain unchanged.
Let us know if you have any questions!
Cheers,

Exa Team

messages.subject: [Correction] Updated list of your inactive OAuth clients list
messages.full_content:
Google Developers logo



Review your corrected list of inactive OAuth clients for accuracy.



Hello Google Developer,

We're writing to inform you that this serves as a correction to the  
communication you might have received on May 28, 2025, titled “[Action  
Advised] Manage your unused OAuth clients and protect your information.”

There was an issue with our recipient list that caused some developers to  
receive incorrect information. This communication incorrectly included some  
of your OAuth clients that have not been inactive for at least five months,  
and will not be deleted.

If you received the previous communication, please disregard it. We  
sincerely apologize for any confusion this may have caused.

Please refer to the message below which you should have received.


We're writing to inform you about an upcoming change that may affect your  
applications and scripts using Google Auth Platform for Sign-in with Google  
or for calling Google APIs.

What you need to know

As we recently announced, starting June 2025, OAuth clients that have  
remained inactive for six months will be automatically deleted. This change  
helps prevent credential theft and misuse.

Inactivity is determined based on the absence of token exchanges and client  
updates. Viewing an OAuth client on Google Cloud Console is not considered  
activity. After an OAuth client is deleted, you will have 30 days to  
restore it in the Google Auth Platform section of the Google Cloud Console.

Impacted OAuth clients

The following OAuth clients that you manage have been inactive for at least  
five months. These will be deleted in a month unless you take action:


avid-truth-434123-e0 (167887354208)

167887354208-cqd79gqkenm4cdf825in2ci9pqdthf9g.apps.googleusercontent.com


What you need to do

Manage your unused clients

To prevent deletion of clients you wish to retain, initiate a Sign-in with  
Google flow or exchange a refresh token for an access token for each client  
listed above.

If you no longer need these clients, no action is required from you. They  
will be deleted automatically after six months of inactivity. You will have  
up to 30 days to restore them in the Google Cloud Console.

Protect your applications

To protect your applications and enhance security, please adhere to the  
following best practices:


Never check client secrets into version control systems, especially those  
that allow access to user data or other production systems
Never share client secrets widely on the internet
Rotate client secrets periodically and change them immediately, if a data  
breach occurs
Keep your developer contact information current to ensure you receive  
future updates from us


We understand the importance of accurate communication and regret this  
error.

Sincerely,

– The Google Cloud Team




Was this information helpful?

A smiling face A neutral face A sad face


© 2025 Google LLC 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043

You have received this mandatory service announcement to update you about  
important changes to Google services you use.

messages.subject: Updates to our Terms & notification of new sub-processors
messages.full_content:
Hi Rich,


We're writing to inform you about updates to our Terms, our Data Processing Agreement and our Sub-processors.

 

Key updates to our Terms & Data Processions Agreement:

- Updated our Data Processing Description to reference all types of data that Customers can upload to Softr
- Clarified that data is only processed by AI-Tools if you choose to use AI-Tools in the platform
- Clarified the liability provisions in the Data Processing Agreement


In addition we have updated the list of Softr's sub-processors. To support the delivery of our Services, Softr Platforms GmbH may engage and use data processors with access to certain Customer Data and this shall serve as notification that the following sub-processors will be added to support AI services **effective from June 21, 2025**:

- OpenAI, LLC
- Anthropic, PBC
- Google Cloud EMEA Ltd

The use of AI-powered tools are opt-in features. If you choose not to use AI-powered tools, no data will be shared with these sub-processors. 

Please note that the changes will not affect the pricing or the way we provide our services to you. For your convenience, we have made a version of the amended document available on our website via these links.
 

Terms & Conditions: https://www.softr.io/terms

Data Processing Agreement: https://www.softr.io/dpa-v1

 

Thank you very much for your continued support!

Best regards,

Softr team
